finding.claim: The /rss endpoint fetches an arbitrary URL taken from the query string and returns the first 400 bytes of the response. An attacker can reach internal services, cloud metadata endpoints and localhost. The response body is reflected, so this is a full read SSRF.

trace.note: params[:u] is passed directly to URI.open, which fetches http/https/ftp URLs, then .read
first 400 bytes of the fetched body are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or IP validation, no allowlist, no private-range blocking, no redirect restrictions. Nothing sits between the source and the sink. The TRUSTED allowlist is applied only in /trusted, not here.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes unvalidated params[:u] from the unauthenticated GET /rss handler (app.rb:7) to URI.open(...).read, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes. The TRUSTED allowlist is only applied in /trusted (app.rb:14).
